akhfash:1-1.t: He said ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ غَرْقاً﴾: He swore — and Allah knows best — upon ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ﴾. And if you wish, you make it upon ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ [6] ﴿قُلُوبٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاجِفَةٌ﴾ [8] ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ﴾. And if you wish, you make ﴿وَٱلنَّازِعَاتِ﴾ (sworn) for ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ ٱلرَّاجِفَةُ﴾ ﴿تَتْبَعُهَا ٱلرَّادِفَةُ﴾ [7], the lām having been dropped. And it is as He, exalted be His mention, said, and as He willed it to be, in this and in all matters.

akhfash:10-11.t: And He said ﴿أَإِنَّا لَمَرْدُودُونَ فِي ٱلْحَافِرَةِ﴾ ﴿أَإِذَا كُنَّا عِظَاماً﴾: as if He meant "shall we be returned when we are bones?" (أَنُرَدُّ إِذَا كُنَّا عِظاماً). As for whoever said ﴿أاِنَّا﴾ and ﴿أَاإِذا كنا﴾ with the two hamzas together, separating them with an alif, he has only left implied the statement for which this was made an adverb (ẓarf), because it had been said to them "you will be raised and brought back" (إِنَّكُم تُبْعَثون وتُعادُون), so they said ﴿أإِذا كنا ترابا﴾ — at that time we will be brought back? This is part of the speech of the Arabs. Some of them say ﴿أَيِنَّا﴾ and ﴿أَيِذَا﴾, lightening the second (hamza), because two hamzas do not come together. The Kufans say "أإِنا" and "أَإِذا", combining the two hamzas. Ibn Abī Isḥāq used to combine the two hamzas in recitation, according to what has reached us. And some Arabs say "اللهمَّ اغفر لي خطائِئى" ("O Allah, forgive me my sins"), pronouncing both with hamza; this is rare, and it is in the dialect of Qays.

akhfash:16-16.t:
And He said ﴿بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾: whoever does not make it fully declinable (treating it as a diptote) makes it (the name of) a town or a tract of land; whoever makes it declinable makes it the name of a valley or a place. And some said: "No, rather it is declinable, and by ﴿طوى﴾ He means only a ṭuwan (a part) of the night", because you say "جِئْتُكَ بعدَ طُوًى من الليل" ("I came to you after a part of the night had passed"). And it is also said ﴿طِوىً﴾ with tanwīn, like "الثِّنى". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-seventh verse cited as evidence]:
تَرى ثِنانَا إِذَا ما جاءَ بَدْأَهُمُ * وَبَدَأَهُم إِن أَتَانَا كانَ ثِنْياَنَا
(You see our second-rank man, when he comes, as their foremost; and their foremost, if he comes to us, is our second-rank.)
And الثِّنى*: it is the thing that is doubled (repeated).

akhfash:25-25.t: And He said ﴿فَأَخَذَهُ ٱللَّهُ نَكَالَ ٱلآخِرَةِ وَٱلأُوْلَىٰ﴾ because when He said ﴿أَخَذَه﴾ it is as if (He said) "He made an exemplary punishment of him" (نَكَّلَ لِهِ), so He brought the maṣdar (verbal noun) out accordingly. And you say "والله لأصْرِمَنَّكَ تركا بَيِّناً" ("by Allah, I will surely cut you off — a clear abandonment"). «[Translator's note: «نَكَّلَ لِهِ» is so written in the source; presumably «نَكَّلَ بِهِ».]»
